chapter: Riddick band and the Fern dances
title: Routine at the Fern: four-minute slow drags and repertoire
summary: Sal explains the ticket slow-drag routine at the Fern, the piano players, and tunes such as Tin Roof, Panama and High Society.

blocks.x: What about the Fern? What kind of numbers did you play at the Fern?

Well, the fine. Well, four minutes slow drag is, you know, the routine was this. Every fourth piece, everybody get a rest. The piano would play. The piano play. I could probably never play there. I could probably name any member piano player. We played there. Almond Hook, Eddie Shields, Von Hecht, Mickey Markle, Ernest Bobby. And we played. And we played. Walls just by itself. Just piano, see. And then now I stop. Four minutes slow drag. And we play. Ten rules. We can stop. We had the band. Yeah, the band. We had the band to play. We were talking about those slow drags. Yeah. Just the end of this one. Yeah.
You want to, what happened, the routine at the Fern? You had those four minute slow drags on?

Yeah. And then we played. We played like a, what's it called? In those days they called it a four-minute slow drag. And everybody go buy a bunch of tickets and then we start playing music like, like Tin Roof. Mm-hm. Panama and Diplomar, High Society, Dixiel and One Step, Muscat Rambles, the same old menu, jazz, and for slow tunes like I'll Get By, and what's the name of it, Five Domino and I'll make records, Rock and Moon records, Blueberry, but another one too, Anchor Suite, oh so many tunes.
What about waltzes? How many waltzes would you play?
